headline: No documented interaction pathways; both docs-only, non-runnable data-engineering artifacts with no shared I/O or egress surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile exposes a shared communication channel, writable filesystem, clipboard, or MCP surface. Agent A is a non-runnable course repo and Agent B is a non-runnable Taipy project; with no ingest path between them, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later deployed with a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge, injection risk becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator forwards one agent's raw output into the other as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared paste/clipboard bridges.
Disable any future shared MCP or message-queue connector.
Review orchestrator wiring before enabling cross-agent handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any future inter-agent channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents report network_egress:none and no data classes touched, so there is no documented path for one agent to exfiltrate the other's data. The pair is docs-only and unverified, but the profiles do not show a shared workspace or sensitive data flow.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk may appear.
IF network egress is enabled on either agent, outbound disclosure becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled on both agents.
Do not mount a shared sensitive workspace.
Separate credentials and local storage per agent.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls before any shared storage is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surfaces, network scopes, or concurrency model are documented for either agent. Agent A and Agent B both show empty io_surfaces and empty concurrency_model, so a write conflict pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, conflicts can emerge.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the current setup.
Avoid mounting the same writable directory into both agents.
Introduce locking before any shared mutable resource is enabled.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks for future shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where Agent A's output is consumed by Agent B as authoritative input, and neither profile shows downstream action authority. With both agents non-runnable and no evidence bundle, cascading error is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding Agent A outputs directly into Agent B without verification, the risk changes.
IF Agent B is later configured to take actions from A's text, downstream errors can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step between agents.
Do not auto-forward outputs from A into B.
Log and review any future handoff format.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent messages.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. Because the profiles are silent on PHI, EU PII, or retention policy, there is no compliance mismatch to assess from the available evidence.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, compliance review is required.
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter residency or retention regime than the other, mismatch risk may appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair until policies are defined.
Document residency and retention before deployment.
Assign separate compliance owners for each agent.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement if regulated data will flow.
